trace.code: if((0x0a == *hd) || (0x0d == *hd)) {   // end-of-headers decided from the FIRST byte only; "\rX-Bad: a<NUL>b\r\n" passes
curlx_dyn_addn(&last_header, hd, hdlen);   // the ENTIRE line (post-CR payload, NUL, bare CR) is copied
http_write_header(data, last_hd, last_hd_len);   // out: label — writes the terminator line to CLIENTWRITE_HEADER WITHOUT Curl_verify_header()
result = Curl_verify_header(data, hd, hdlen);   // ordinary headers go through this; NUL/spurious-CR -> CURLE_WEIRD_SERVER_REPLY
FIX (3f68448): require the terminator to be exactly "\n" (len 1) or "\r\n" (len 2), else return CURLE_WEIRD_SERVER_REPLY

preconditions: the attacker controls HTTP/1.1 (or RTSP) response bytes — a malicious/compromised origin, a MITM inside a trusted CA, or a hostile origin reached through SSRF
the victim consumes headers via CURLOPT_HEADERFUNCTION, `curl -D <file>`, or `curl -i` (documented header sinks)
no non-default option, no --insecure, no privileged role required

evidence.vulnerable_version: curl <= 8.23.0 (latest release 2026-10-14); the bug is live in 8.23.0 and all prior releases
evidence.fixed_version: master @ 3f68448 (2026-11-10, "http: reject malformed header terminators") — NOT yet in any release
evidence.observed_result:
The C reproducer ports the line-splitting (memchr '

real_exploit.target: curl 8.23.0 lib/http.c http_rw_hd() / http_on_response() — the terminator-line path that skips Curl_verify_header(), ported verbatim; the reporter (christos-cantina-security, issue #23859) confirmed the identical bytes against a real 8.23.1-DEV libcurl build with a loopback TCP server (nothing mocked)
real_exploit.backend: zig cc (C99, stdlib) — faithful port of the line-splitter, the vulnerable vs fixed terminator classification, and the NUL/CR verify_header rejection; the crafted response's injected bytes are delivered to a modeled header sink exactly as http_write_header -> CLIENTWRITE_HEADER does
real_exploit.demonstrated: A malicious origin sends "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n" + "\rX-Bad: a\0b\r\n"; the vulnerable parser treats the CR-prefixed line as the end-of-headers terminator and writes the full 13 bytes (leading 0d, embedded 00) to the header sink with transfer result 0 (CURLE_OK) — bypassing the NUL/CR rejection that ordinary headers and chunked trailers receive. The fixed parser rejects the line with CURLE_WEIRD_SERVER_REPLY (8) and delivers nothing. A NUL in a normal header line is rejected by both. CWE-436/116 header-validation bypass.

evidence.notes: Honest impact is a parser-validation / hardening bypass: a server that already controls the response can push NUL / bare-CR / arbitrary payload through the end-of-headers terminator line into CURLOPT_HEADERFUNCTION / -D / -i on a transfer that still returns CURLE_OK. curl itself suffers no confidentiality/integrity/availability loss — it faithfully delivers bytes to a documented, length-delimited, non-NUL-terminated sink; no memory-safety, credential-leak, cross-origin, or request-smuggling impact (reporter verified ASan-clean, byte-identical output), and curl_easy_header() is unaffected (the headers collector drops CR/LF-prefixed lines). Concrete harm requires a downstream consumer that treats the buffer as a C string or trusts the separator line as a record boundary (hence AC:H and LOW severity). This bypasses the invariant introduced by curl commits 526e0ef4cb (reject NUL in headers) and c3c2cfb65d (reject spurious CR). Reported by christos-cantina-security (issue #23859); fixed on master 2026-11-10 (3f68448), unreleased (latest release 8.23.0, 2026-10-14).
